title: Unpivot Quarterly Columns to Rows Using UNION ALL
description:
Transform a wide table with one column per quarter into a long/tall format (one row per quarter per employee) using UNION ALL.

**Table: quarterly_sales** — `employee`, `q1`, `q2`, `q3`, `q4`

Output columns: `employee`, `quarter`, `sales`. Order by `employee`, `quarter`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE quarterly_sales (employee VARCHAR, q1 INT, q2 INT, q3 INT, q4 INT); INSERT INTO quarterly_sales VALUES ('Alice',12000,15000,18000,14000),('Bob',9000,11000,10000,13000),('Carol',20000,22000,25000,21000);
solution_sql: SELECT employee, 'Q1' AS quarter, q1 AS sales FROM quarterly_sales UNION ALL SELECT employee, 'Q2', q2 FROM quarterly_sales UNION ALL SELECT employee, 'Q3', q3 FROM quarterly_sales UNION ALL SELECT employee, 'Q4', q4 FROM quarterly_sales ORDER BY employee, quarter

test_cases.description: 3 employees × 4 quarters = 12 rows in the unpivoted output

hints: Each UNION ALL block targets a single quarter column, returning a literal string for the quarter name and the column value as sales.
UNION ALL (not UNION) is correct here — all rows are intentionally distinct; UNION would do unnecessary deduplication work.
explanation: There is no single UNPIVOT keyword in standard SQL. Instead, write one SELECT per quarter column with a literal 'Q1', 'Q2' etc. label, then UNION ALL them together. 3 employees × 4 UNIONed blocks = 12 rows. This is the portable way to reshape wide data into long format.
